task.title: Give empty scene openers a valid private beat-planner request
task.source: Live Pi report that a newly generated /scene opener still read as AI-shaped prose
task.classification: engine generation, prompt assembly, provider compatibility, and cross-entrypoint parity

coreClaim: A generated /scene opener with no saved transcript gives the private Agent beat planner the ephemeral opening intent as a terminal user message, so the plan succeeds and reaches the configured Roleplay writer.
rootCause: The planner built its request only from persisted chat messages. A new /scene chat has none, so the OpenAI ChatGPT adapter stripped the system-only request into instructions plus an empty input array; the provider returned HTTP 400 and the bounded planner correctly but silently fell back to the baseline writer prompt.

inScope: Ephemeral generation-guide and current-user intent passed to the private planner
Normal, dry-run, and direct-message Roleplay generation parity
Terminal-user fallback for other empty Roleplay planner requests
outOfScope: Changing the configured Agent or writer model
Adding another visible writer or post-generation rewrite
Guaranteeing every provider sample passes StoryScope

claimBoundary.coreClaim: The configured Agent model receives a valid planning request and its bounded beat guidance is injected into the existing configured writer call.
claimBoundary.riskType: prompt role ordering, model-call routing, and cross-entrypoint compatibility
entrypoints: Generated /scene opening with an empty transcript
legacyPathsOrFormats: Saved user messages continue to supply planner history
Chats without active Narrative Craft remain unchanged
Providers other than openai_chatgpt keep the same agent execution contract
outOfScopeClaims: No claim that the private Agent call has zero latency.
No claim that StoryScope deterministically grades every sample.
No claim that Conversation or Game modes use this planner.

contractLaneGate.brokenContract: The /scene workflow activated Narrative Craft but its empty new chat produced a system-only Agent request that the configured OpenAI Responses provider could not execute.
contractLaneGate.producer: src/engine/generation/start-generation.ts owns the ephemeral current request passed into the agent runtime.
contractLaneGate.consumer: src/engine/generation/agent-runner.ts owns the private Roleplay beat-planner request consumed before the visible writer call.
contractLaneGate.impliedContract: A private planner request must contain usable model input even when the visible chat has no persisted messages yet.
contractLaneGate.actualEnforcement: All Roleplay generation paths pass ephemeral intent into the runtime; the planner appends it as a user message or supplies a bounded terminal-user task when history ends without one.
contractLaneGate.primaryOwnerDetail: The TypeScript generation engine owns request assembly, agent routing, and writer injection.
contractLaneGate.wrongLaneFixToAvoid: Do not special-case the UI, relax the provider adapter, add a second writer, or swallow another invalid planner request.
regressionProof: The agent-runner regression failed before the fix because the captured request ended on a system message instead of the scene intent.
The request-level dry-run regression proves an empty transcript sends the opening intent to the Agent and the returned private beat reaches the writer prompt.

positiveRows.claim: An empty /scene opener gives the Agent provider usable input.
positiveRows.evidence: The focused agent-runner test asserts the request's final message is user-role and contains the planned opening beat.

positiveRows.claim: Nano remains the visible writer and receives the successful private plan.
positiveRows.evidence: The request-level dry-run test observes the Agent connection first, the configured writer connection second, and Private beat plan in the writer prompt.

contradictionRows.claim: The repair must not require a persisted fake user chat message.
contradictionRows.evidence: The runtime-only instruction is added to AgentContext and never written to storage or the visible transcript.

contradictionRows.claim: The provider adapter must not accept input-less requests globally.
contradictionRows.evidence: The fix is confined to the Roleplay beat planner, where the task input is semantically required.

legacyDefaultRows.claim: Existing saved-message Roleplay planning remains valid.
legacyDefaultRows.evidence: The existing configured-Agent beat-plan test and Narrative Craft request-level suite remain green.

legacyDefaultRows.claim: Conversation and Game behavior remain mode-separated.
legacyDefaultRows.evidence: Only the Roleplay-only beat-plan call consumes the new field; no Conversation or Game owner files changed.

untestedRows: A post-deploy user-created live /scene sample is not generated automatically because doing so would alter the user's chat history and incur provider cost.

ownedFacts.description: The reported Pi opener's private planner failed before the visible writer began.
ownedFacts.evidence: Pi runtime logs recorded HTTP 400: one of input, previous_response_id, prompt, or conversation_id must be provided.

ownedFacts.description: The visible writer remained Nano/GLM 5.2 while the private planner selected the configured Agent default.
ownedFacts.evidence: Read-only Pi connection and agent configuration inspection on the reported chat.

ownedFacts.description: The production JavaScript bundle remains inside its enforced budget.
ownedFacts.evidence: pnpm perf:size measured 1724.6 KiB gzip against the 1726.0 KiB total-JS limit.

manualBlockers.item: Provider prose quality varies by sample
manualBlockers.reason: The deterministic bug is the rejected planner request and missing guidance, not a guarantee about a stochastic detector score.
